subject: zoology_2
question_text: If you take butter in your food, how does it get digested and absorbed in the body? Explain.

mark_split.label: Butter is a fat, digested in the small intestine

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.29, SAQ 13. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revised 2026-09-05: s1's first common mistake and memory tip called any fat digestion outside the small intestine an error, although the gastric glands do secrete a small amount of lipase, so both now say almost all of it happens in the small intestine; the insider note no longer says half the answer goes unmarked.

insider_note: The question has two halves and equal marks for each. Write digestion and absorption under two headings so both halves are on the page.

steps.label: Butter is a fat
steps.why: The question is a fat question in disguise, so the first line has to name butter as a lipid and place its digestion in the small intestine.
common_mistakes: Placing the main digestion of fat in the mouth or stomach. Almost all of it happens in the small intestine, with bile salts and pancreatic lipase.
Treating butter as a protein because it comes from milk.
steps.memory_tip: Butter is fat, so its digestion belongs to the small intestine.
steps.margin_note: Two lines. Say what butter is and where it is digested.
lines: Butter is a fat, that is, a lipid.
It is digested only in the small intestine.

steps.label: Bile salts and lipase
steps.why: Fat does not mix with water, so it must first be broken into tiny droplets before a water-soluble enzyme can reach its surface.
common_mistakes: Writing that bile digests fat. Bile emulsifies fat; lipase digests it.
Leaving out the products. Lipase gives fatty acids and glycerol.
steps.memory_tip: Bile breaks the fat into drops, lipase breaks the drops into pieces.
steps.margin_note: Emulsify is the marking word. Use it.
lines: Bile juice contains bile salts. They
emulsify fats into very small micelles.
Bile also activates lipase.
Lipase converts emulsified fats into fatty
acids and glycerol.

steps.label: Micelles and chylomicrons
steps.why: Fatty acids cannot dissolve in blood plasma, so they are repacked twice: first as micelles to cross the cell, then as chylomicrons to travel.
common_mistakes: Writing that fatty acids pass straight into the blood. They cannot.
Mixing up micelles and chylomicrons. Micelles come first, inside the gut.
steps.memory_tip: Micelle to get in, chylomicron to travel out.
steps.margin_note: Both names carry marks. Keep them in order.
lines: Fatty acids and glycerol are insoluble in
water, so they cannot enter the blood
directly.
They are first modified into small micelles,
which move into intestinal mucosal cells.
There they are reformed into protein coated
fat globules called chylomicrons.

steps.label: Lymph to blood
steps.why: Fat is the one food that reaches the blood by the lymph route instead of the hepatic portal vein, and that is the point of the question.
common_mistakes: Sending chylomicrons into blood capillaries. They enter lymph capillaries.
Stopping at the blood. Say where the fat finally goes.
steps.memory_tip: Fat takes the lymph road, not the blood road.
steps.margin_note: End with storage in adipose tissue and liver.
lines: Chylomicrons are carried into the lymph
capillaries of the villi.
The lymph vessels release them into the
blood stream.
The enzyme lipoprotein lipase breaks them
down again to fatty acids and glycerol.

lines.text: Stored in adipose tissue and in the liver
